page: Microsoft Azure DC16es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon TDX processor. The configuration allocates 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 execution, and SHA-NI cryptographic support. No integrated GPUs or local storage devices are bundled with this instance type, requiring external remote block storage.

Benchmark testing reflects strong single-core performance alongside average multi-core and memory throughput. The server registered a Geekbench single-core score of 1944.0, positioning it in the upper quartile of comparable instances. Multi-core results remained mid-tier, yielding 11137.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 14092.2 in multi-core stress-ng tests. PassMark testing generated a CPU score of 23118.53, an extended instructions score of 18731.6, and a database operations metric of 6467.49. In-memory throughput showed relative weakness with a PassMark memory score of 1371.4, while Redis SET performance reached 18.44 million operations per second.

The hardware configuration offers predictable single-threaded compute density and hardware-accelerated matrix operations. Tradeoffs include the lack of ephemeral local storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies on attached network storage. With its 1:4 resource allocation and dedicated core access, this server configuration fits CI/CD compilation jobs, enterprise application tiers, backend web serving, and relational database hosting.
